_about: KAIRO daily quizzes, pilot week 1. 10 questions, 5 minutes, opens 06:00 WAT, never closes, unranked, answers shown right after submitting. Every key below is the official source key and was independently re-solved before writing the explanation. 'fix' corrects transcription errors in the source text (stem = new question text, options = replaced option texts).

questions.explanation: Adjacent compression and rarefaction are half a wavelength apart, so λ = 2 × 17 cm = 34 cm = 0.34 m. f = v/λ = 340/0.34 = 1000 Hz. Trap: using 17 cm as the full wavelength gives 2000 Hz, which is not an option, so students then guess.

fix.stem: When an ebonite rod is rubbed with fur, it has

questions.explanation: Rubbing transfers electrons from the fur to the ebonite, so the ebonite gains electrons and becomes negatively charged (the fur becomes positive). Trap: a glass rod rubbed with silk is the one that becomes positive.

In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, so the centripetal acceleration v²/r has a constant size, but it always points towards the centre, so its direction keeps changing. Trap: 'uniform speed' tempts students to say there is no acceleration or that it is fully constant.
Frequency does not change when light enters glass, so the wavelength shrinks by the refractive index: λ = 5000 × 10⁻⁸ cm ÷ 1.5 = 3333 × 10⁻⁸ cm. Trap: multiplying by 1.5 (7500) instead of dividing.

Work = force × distance moved in the direction of the force. Holding the stone still means it moves no distance, so no work is done, however long it is held. Trap: mgh is the energy it already has (potential energy), not work done while holding it.

fix.stem: Determine the distance between two consecutive antinodes if the wavelength is 60cm

questions.explanation: In a stationary wave, consecutive antinodes (or nodes) are half a wavelength apart: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm. Trap: choosing 60 cm. A node and the next antinode are only a quarter wavelength (15 cm) apart.

Refractive index n = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed in the material = (3 × 10⁸) ÷ (2.4 × 10⁸) = 1.25. Trap: dividing the other way gives 0.8, and 1.33 is the familiar value for water, not the answer here.

Distance in the nth second: s = u + ½a(2n − 1) = 0 + ½ × 6 × (2 × 3 − 1) = 3 × 5 = 15 m. Trap: 27 m is the total distance covered in 3 seconds (½ × 6 × 3²), not the distance in the third second alone.

The threshold frequency is f₀ = W/h, where W is the work function of the photocathode metal, so it depends only on the material. Trap: intensity changes the number of electrons emitted, not the threshold; the incident frequency is what gets compared with the threshold.

A stretched string gives all harmonics: 40, 80, 120, 160 Hz and so on. Between 40 Hz and 150 Hz lie 80 Hz and 120 Hz, which are the 1st and 2nd overtones, so there are 2. Trap: counting 40 Hz itself. The fundamental is not an overtone.
Total of the proportions = 1 + 4 + 6 + 7 = 18. Angle = 7/18 × 360° = 140°. Trap: 120° is the sector for 6, not 7.
After the first child takes ¼, ¾ remains. The second takes ¾ of that remainder: ¾ × ¾ = 9/16. The third gets ¾ − 9/16 = 12/16 − 9/16 = 3/16. Trap: 9/16 is the second child's share, not the third's.
There are 6 + 5 + 7 = 18 shirts and 7 are purple, so P(purple) = 7/18. Trap: 7/11 compares purple with the non-purple shirts instead of with all shirts.

Let John have x. After giving x/3 away he has 2x/3, and Janet has 105 + x/3. Then 2x/3 = ¼(105 + x/3), so 8x/3 = 105 + x/3, which gives 7x/3 = 105 and x = ₦45. Check: John gives ₦15, keeps ₦30; Janet has ₦120, and ¼ of 120 = 30. ✓
2 = 1×2, 6 = 2×3, 12 = 3×4, 20 = 4×5, so the nth term is n(n + 1) = n² + n. Trap: 4n − 2 fits the first two terms only. Always test a formula on at least three terms.
The numerator is a difference of two squares: [(2m − u) − (m − 2u)][(2m − u) + (m − 2u)] = (m + u)(3m − 3u) = 3(m + u)(m − u). The denominator is 5(m² − u²) = 5(m − u)(m + u). Cancelling leaves 3/5.
Total surface area of a solid cone = πr² + πrl = π(2√3)² + π(2√3)(4√3) = 12π + 24π = 36π cm². Trap: 24π is only the curved surface. A solid cone also has its circular base.
P(white) on one throw = 4/6 = 2/3. The two throws are independent, so P(white both times) = 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9. Trap: adding the probabilities instead of multiplying them.
The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. 'At least one head' is every outcome except TT: 1 − ¼ = ¾. Trap: ½ is the chance of exactly one head.

x − 2y + 4 = 0 gives y = ½x + 2, so PQ has gradient ½. A perpendicular line has gradient −2. Through (1, −1): y + 1 = −2(x − 1), so y = −2x + 1, i.e. 2x + y − 1 = 0. Trap: 2x + y − 3 = 0 has the right gradient but does not pass through (1, −1).
'If only… could have avoided' refers to an unreal past situation, which needs the past perfect: 'If only Adoyi had known…'. Trap: 'knew' is used for unreal present wishes ('If only he knew now').
'Not disallowed' means the goal stood, so the forward must have been onside, i.e. very well positioned. Trap: 'in an off-side position' would make the goal disallowed. Watch the double negative.
To decline something is to refuse it, so the opposite is 'accepted'. Trap: 'rejected' has the same meaning as declined, not the opposite.
'Enervating' means draining your energy, so the opposite is 'invigorating' (energising). Trap: 'enervating' sounds like 'energising', which is why 'an energy sapping' (a synonym) catches students.

To agree with a negative statement in English you answer with a negative: 'No, I won't.' Trap: 'Yes, I won't' mixes a positive answer with a negative verb, and 'No, I will not visit' is over-long and unidiomatic.

'Hear' is a stative verb (a sense verb), so it is not normally used in the continuous form. Use 'can hear' for ability in the present. Trap: 'am hearing' sounds natural in Nigerian speech but is wrong here.
Missing property that is found and returned is 'recovered'. Trap: 'found' is close but 'recovered' is the precise word for getting back stolen or lost items.
Inclinations are things you naturally like or lean towards, so the opposite is 'aversions' (strong dislikes). Trap: 'dispositions' and 'impulses' are near-synonyms of inclinations.
A 'showdown' is a final, decisive confrontation, which fits a rematch after last season's defeat. Trap: 'show-off' (boasting) and 'show up' (arrive) are real phrasal verbs with different meanings.
The fixed expression is 'contrary to', meaning opposed to. Trap: 'inconsistent' needs 'with', and 'different' needs 'from', so neither fits 'to'.
At balance, R₁/R₂ = l/(100 − l), so 2/3 = l/(100 − l). Then 200 − 2l = 3l, giving l = 40 cm. Trap: 60 cm is the length from the right-hand end.

Conduction and convection both need a material medium. A vacuum has none, so it cuts both. Radiation crosses a vacuum and is reduced by the silvered walls instead. Trap: 'radiation' answers are about the silvering, not the vacuum.

An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (mass 4, charge 2), so the nucleus loses 4 in mass number and 2 in atomic number. Statement iii contradicts i, so 'i and ii only'. Trap: beta decay is the one where the mass number does not change.

Terylene (a polyester) forms when the diol and the dicarboxylic acid join and give off water each time, which is a condensation polymerisation. Trap: polythene and PVC are addition polymers; anything that gives off a small molecule like water is condensation.
Kerosine (paraffin) is the fraction used as aviation (jet) fuel. Trap: gasoline (petrol) is for cars; diesel is for heavy engines.

Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√(molar mass), so time ∝ √M. t(H₂)/t(O₂) = √(2/32) = ¼, so t = 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5 s. Trap: using atomic masses (1 and 16) instead of molecular masses (2 and 32). The ratio happens to be the same here, but always use molecules for gases.
Moles of sugar = 34.2 ÷ 342 = 0.1 mol in 50 cm³. Per dm³: 0.1 × (1000/50) = 2.0 mol dm⁻³. Trap: forgetting to scale from 50 cm³ to 1000 cm³ gives 0.1.

Savanna trees have thick, corky (flaky) bark that protects them from the frequent bush fires and dry season. Trap: thin smooth bark belongs to rainforest trees, and seedlings on the mother plant (vivipary) belong to mangroves.

Coelenterates (Hydra, jellyfish) have a single body cavity, the enteron, and no true coelom. Molluscs, reptiles and arthropods all have a coelom (reduced in some). Trap: confusing 'coelenterata' with 'coelom' because the names look alike.

Salt concentration is the main difference between marine and fresh water, and most aquatic animals can tolerate only one, so salinity controls where they live. Trap: pH, current and turbidity vary within both habitats and are secondary.
'Recent' is an adjective, so 'they are recent' is correct. Trap: 'of recent' is a common Nigerian error. 'Of late' is fine, 'of recent' is not.

One past action (conceding two goals, in the past perfect) was followed by another, so the second takes the simple past: 'their enthusiasm began to wane'. Trap: 'had begun to wane' wrongly places the waning before the goals.
'Sting' is irregular: sting, stung, stung. The passive needs the past participle: 'are stung'. Trap: 'stinged' and 'stang' are not standard English.
The outer parts of a town are its 'outskirts', a plural-only noun. Trap: 'outskirt' (no s) is wrong, and 'outstretch' is a verb.
Let y = 6ˣ. Then 6^(2x+1) = 6 × (6ˣ)² = 6y², so the expression is 6y² + 7y − 5 = (3y + 5)(2y − 1) = [3(6ˣ) + 5][2(6ˣ) − 1]. Check by expanding: 6y² − 3y + 10y − 5 ✓.

fix.stem: What is the circumference of latitude θ°S if R is the radius of the earth?

questions.explanation: The radius of the circle of latitude θ is R cos θ, so its circumference is 2πR cos θ. This works for north or south latitudes. Trap: R cos θ is the radius, not the circumference, and sin is for the angle from the pole.
A closed pipe's fundamental has length L = λ/4, and λ = v/f = 340/170 = 2 m, so L = 0.5 m = 50 cm. Trap: using L = λ/2 (the open-pipe formula) gives 100 cm.

fix.stem: A transverse wave is applied to a string whose mass per unit length is 3 x 10^-2 kgm^-1. If the string is under a tension of 12N, the speed of propagation of the wave is

questions.explanation: Wave speed on a string: v = √(T/μ) = √(12 ÷ 0.03) = √400 = 20 m s⁻¹. Trap: forgetting the square root gives 400.
Perfumes are dissolved in ethanol (C₂H₅OH), which dissolves the scented oils and evaporates quickly on the skin. Trap: ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) is vinegar.

fix.stem: Lung books are used for respiration in

questions.explanation: Spiders (arachnids) breathe with lung books, which are stacks of thin plates like the pages of a book. Trap: insects and millipedes breathe through tracheae, not lung books.

Leaded petrol contains lead compounds, and sucking petrol by mouth lets lead into the body, where it builds up in the blood and damages the nerves and kidneys. Trap: iron, calcium and magnesium are useful minerals, not petrol contaminants.

Sodium hydroxide plus copper(II) sulphate is the Biuret test, and a violet/purple colour shows protein. Trap: reducing sugars use Fehling's or Benedict's (brick-red), starch uses iodine (blue-black), fats use Sudan III or the grease spot.

The caterpillar (larva) is the feeding stage of a butterfly and eats leaves, so it does the crop damage. Trap: maggots are fly larvae, nymphs belong to incomplete metamorphosis (e.g. grasshoppers), and the pupa does not feed.

fix.stem: Women rarely suffer from colour blindness because

questions.explanation: The colour-blindness gene is recessive and carried on the X chromosome. A man (XY) with one affected X is colour-blind, but a woman (XX) needs the gene on both X chromosomes, which is rare. Trap: women can be colour-blind, so 'only men are colour blind' is false.

fix.stem: In a dicotyledonous stem, each companion cell is found beside the

questions.explanation: Companion cells sit beside the sieve tube elements in the phloem and keep them alive, since sieve tubes have no nucleus. Trap: xylem vessels are dead tubes with no companion cells.
A saprophyte (e.g. a fungus or bacterium of decay) feeds on dead organic matter, so no second living organism is involved. Commensalism, parasitism and symbiosis all involve two living organisms.

Numbers fall at each step up the food chain because energy is lost at every trophic level, so the top (tertiary) consumers are the fewest. Trap: producers form the broad base, so they are the most numerous.
In dim light photosynthesis slows until it can just balance respiration (the compensation point), so there is no net gas exchange. Trap: respiration never stops in a living plant.

In this mutualism the plant gives the Rhizobium bacteria shelter (the nodule) and carbohydrates from photosynthesis, and the bacteria fix nitrogen for the plant. Trap: minerals and nitrogen flow from the bacteria to the plant, not the other way.
Genes, the units of inheritance, are found on chromosomes in the nucleus. Trap: ribosomes make proteins from the genetic code, but the genes themselves are on the chromosomes.

Nitrogen is made in the laboratory by warming sodium dioxonitrate(III) (sodium nitrite) with ammonium chloride: NaNO₂ + NH₄Cl → NaCl + 2H₂O + N₂. Trap: dioxonitrate(V) is wrong; the (III) salt is the nitrite.
Protons = atomic number = 17. Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 36 − 17 = 19. Trap: confusing the mass number (36) with the number of neutrons.

The titre (volume of soap solution needed) is highest where the most Ca²⁺ is left. Boiling removes temporary hardness but not permanent hardness, so permanently hard water after boiling still holds its Ca²⁺. Trap: permutit (ion exchange) does remove permanent hardness.

How much gas dissolves depends on the solvent, the gas itself (e.g. NH₃ is far more soluble than O₂), the temperature (gases dissolve less when warm) and the pressure (Henry's law). So all four: I, II, III and IV. Trap: pressure matters for gases even though it hardly affects solids.

fix.stem: When water drops are added to calcium carbide in a container and the gas is passed through a jet and lit, the resultant flame is called an?

questions.explanation: Calcium carbide and water give ethyne (acetylene): CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂. Burning ethyne in oxygen gives the very hot oxyacetylene flame used for welding. Trap: 'oxyethylene' refers to ethene, not ethyne.
Adding concentrated HCl raises the hydrogen ion concentration, which makes the solution more acidic, so the pH falls below 3.4. Trap: a lower pH means more acidic.

Saponification (soap making) is the hydrolysis of alkanoates (esters, such as fats and oils) by sodium hydroxide, giving soap plus an alcohol (glycerol for fats). Trap: an acid plus NaOH is neutralisation, not saponification.
Non-cyclic alkanols C₄H₉OH: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol, which is 4. Trap: forgetting the branched chains and answering 2.

Hydrogen bonds are strongest when H is bonded to the most electronegative atom. Fluorine is the most electronegative element, so HF has the strongest hydrogen bonds. Trap: HCl and CH₄ do not form real hydrogen bonds.

Q = It = 500 × 24 × 3600 = 43 200 000 C. Mg²⁺ needs 2 faradays per mole, so moles = 43 200 000 ÷ (2 × 96 500) ≈ 223.8 mol. Mass = 223.8 × 24 ≈ 5372 g ≈ 5.4 kg. Trap: forgetting the 2+ charge doubles the answer (10.8 kg).
